Rashi on Eruvin 69a:10:1.english: Who is an apostate Jew - [Such] that we consider him an apostate with regard to all matters.

Rashi on Eruvin 69a:10:2.hebrew: ר' מאיר ורבנן - במס' בכורות, בפר' עד כמה (בכורות דף ל:):
Rashi on Eruvin 69a:10:2.english: Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis - [Their dispute is found] in tractate Bekhorot, in the chapter [entitled] Ad Kamah (Bekhorot 30b).

Rashi on Eruvin 69a:2:1.english: Say: He does not render it prohibited - According to Rabbi Meir.

Rashi on Eruvin 69a:3:1.english: And it was taught - [This is stated] affirmatively [as a support, and not as an objection].

Rashi on Eruvin 69a:3:2.english: Before he gave, etc. - [The baraita] refers to an Israelite who did not join in an eiruv:

Rashi on Eruvin 69a:3:3.hebrew: יכול לבטל - אע"ג דמומר הוא לחלל שבת, יכול לבטל:
Rashi on Eruvin 69a:3:3.english: He can renounce - Even though he is an apostate with regard to desecrating Shabbat, he can [still] renounce [his rights].

Rashi on Eruvin 69a:3:4.hebrew: במזיד אין יכול לבטל - קסבר ר' יהודה: מחלל שבת אין יכול לבטל בלא שכירות:
Rashi on Eruvin 69a:3:4.english: [If he carried] intentionally, he cannot renounce - Rabbi Yehuda maintains [that] a desecrator of Shabbat cannot renounce [his rights] without leasing [them].

Rashi on Eruvin 69a:4:1.hebrew: אוסר - דהדר שקליה לרשותיה, ובשוגג נמי — קנסו שוגג אטו מזיד:
Rashi on Eruvin 69a:4:1.english: He renders [it] prohibited - For he took back his rights; and in [the case of acting] unwittingly as well, they penalized [one who acts] unwittingly on account of [one who acts] intentionally.

Rashi on Eruvin 69a:4:2.hebrew: במה דברים אמורים - ר"מ קאמר לה, דאילו ר' יהודה, ללישנא דמתני', קאמר דלא מהניא חזקה. וללישנא דברייתא, דקאמר ר' יהודה "עד שלא תחשך", טעמא לאו משום דלא מהניא חזקה הוא, אלא משום דקסבר: הרי הוא כעובד כוכבים; וגבי ישראל שביטל, איכא למימר דאפי' לר' יהודה מהניא חזקה, ו"במה דברים אמורים" — דברי הכל הוא:
Rashi on Eruvin 69a:4:2.english: In what case is this statement said? - Rabbi Meir stated it, for as for Rabbi Yehuda, according to the version of the Mishnah, he maintains that taking possession is of no effect; whereas according to the version of the Baraita, in which Rabbi Yehuda says, “Before night falls,” the reason is not that taking possession is of no effect, but rather because he holds that he is [considered] like an idolater, and regarding a Jew who renounced [his rights], it can be said that even according to Rabbi Yehuda taking possession is effective, and “In what case is this statement said?” is [the opinion of] everyone.

Rashi on Eruvin 69a:5:1.hebrew: והא אנן תנן - לר' יהודה, עד שלא יוציא — אלמא מהני ביטול כל כמה דלא הדר ביה, ובחזקה הוא דפליג, דקסבר לא מהניא:
Rashi on Eruvin 69a:5:1.english: But didn’t we learn - According to Rabbi Yehuda, “before he takes out [his vessels],” which indicates that renunciation is effective as long as he has not retracted it, and it is [only] regarding possession that he disagrees, as he maintains [that possession] is not effective.

Rashi on Eruvin 69a:6:1.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא - מתני' דמשמע צדוקי מבטל — במומר לחלל בצנעא:
Rashi on Eruvin 69a:6:1.english: And if you wish, say - The Mishnah, which implies that a Sadducee may renounce [his rights, refers to] an apostate who desecrates [the Sabbath] in private.

Rashi on Eruvin 69a:7:2.hebrew: מומר הוי - בתמיה: וכי משום גילוי פנים חשיב ליה מומר?:
Rashi on Eruvin 69a:7:2.english: Is he an apostate - [This is asked] in astonishment: Does [the Tanna] consider him an apostate [merely] because of brazenness?

Rashi on Eruvin 69a:8:2.hebrew: כר' יהודה - דלר"מ, מומר לחלל שבת בפרהסיא מבטל:
Rashi on Eruvin 69a:8:2.english: In accordance with Rabbi Yehuda - For according to Rabbi Meir, an apostate who desecrates Shabbat in public may renounce [his rights].

Rashi on Eruvin 69a:9:1.hebrew: בחומרתא דמדושא - טבעת שחותמה ממין אחר. ואמרי' במסכת שבת (דף נט:): היא של אלמוג וחותמה של מתכת, אסור לצאת בה. חומרתא — חותם; מדושא — לא אתפרש. ובדקתי במס' שבת, ולא נשנית שם לענין שבת, אלא לענין טומאה. ואומר אני: חומרתא דמדושא — קשר של בושם, אחד ממיני הבשמים; וכי האי גוונא אמרי' בשבת (דף סב.), דאין יוצאין בחומרתא דפילון, וחייב עליו חטאת, משום דמשאוי הוא ואינו תכשיט אדם:
Rashi on Eruvin 69a:9:1.english: With a chumarta dimdusha - [Some explain:] A ring whose seal is of another material. And we say in Tractate Shabbat (59b): [If] it is of coral and its seal is of metal, it is forbidden to go out with it. [According to this explanation,] chumarta [means] a seal; madusha was not explained. But I checked in Tractate Shabbat, and it was not taught there with regard to Shabbat, but rather with regard to ritual impurity. And I say: Chumarta dimdusha is a knot of perfume, [madusha being] one of the varieties of perfume; and along these lines we say in Shabbat (62a) that one may not go out with a knot of foliatum [chumarta defilyon], and one is liable to a sin-offering on its account because it is a burden and is not an ornament of a person.

Rashi on Eruvin 69a:9:2.english: Such as this - [One] who desecrates Shabbat in private.

Tosafot on Eruvin 69a:10:1.hebrew: אי כר"מ אפי' בא' מכל איסורין נמי - וה"נ תניא בהדיא בבכורות בפ' עד כמה (בכורות ד' ל.): "נחשד לדבר אחד — נחשד לכל התורה כולה", דברי ר"מ. ותימה: דבפ' זה בורר (סנהדרין דף כז.), גבי פלוגתא דאביי ורבא דאוכל נבלות להכעיס ורבא אמר "כשר", בעי לאוקומי רבא כר' יוסי, דאמר: הוזם בדיני ממונות — כשר בדיני נפשות; ומשני: דרבא אפי' כר"מ, דאמר עד זומם פסול לכל התורה כולה — דע"כ לא קאמר ר"מ התם אלא גבי עד זומם דממון, דרע לשמים ולבריות, אבל הכא, דרע לשמים ולא לבריות — לא. שמע מיניה, דלית ליה לר"מ חשוד לאחד מכל האסורין להוי חשוד לכל התורה כולה לרבא, דלא אמר מקילתא לחמירתא אלא בעד זומם דממון דווקא, דרע לשמים ורע לבריות! ומיהו, לאביי דהתם ניחא, וקיי"ל כוותיה. וי"ל, דאפי' לרבא: חשוד לדבר אחד דרע לשמים ולא לבריות — חשוד לכל התורה כולה בכיוצא בה, דרע לשמים ולא לבריות, אפי' מקילתא לחמירתא; וחשוד לדבר אחד דרע לשמים ורע לבריות — חשוד לכל התורה כולה, אפילו רע לשמים ורע לבריות:
Tosafot on Eruvin 69a:10:1.english: "If in accordance with Rabbi Meir, even in one of all prohibitions as well" - And so too it is taught explicitly in Bekhorot, in the chapter [entitled] Ad Kamah (Bekhorot 30a): "One who is suspected of one matter is suspected of the entire Torah," [these are] the words of Rabbi Meir. And it is astonishing: for in the chapter [entitled] Zeh Borer (Sanhedrin 27a), regarding the dispute between Abaye and Rava concerning one who eats carcasses out of defiance, where Rava said [that he is] valid [as a witness], [the Gemara there] seeks to establish Rava in accordance with Rabbi Yose, who said: [A witness who] was proved a conspiring witness in monetary cases is valid in capital cases; and [the Gemara] answers that Rava [can agree] even with Rabbi Meir, who said [that] a conspiring witness is disqualified from [testifying in] the entire Torah — for perforce Rabbi Meir only said [this] there regarding a conspiring witness in monetary matters, which is bad towards Heaven and towards fellow creatures, but here, where it is bad towards Heaven and not towards fellow creatures, no [he is not disqualified]. Learn from this that according to Rava, Rabbi Meir does not hold that one suspected of one of all the prohibitions should be suspected of the entire Torah, for he does not derive [an inference] from a lenient [case] to a stringent [one] except specifically in the case of a conspiring witness in monetary matters, which is bad towards Heaven and bad towards fellow creatures! However, according to Abaye there [it is] well, and we establish the halakhah in accordance with him. And one can say that even according to Rava: one who is suspected of one matter that is bad towards Heaven and not towards fellow creatures is suspected of the entire Torah in that which is similar to it, which is bad towards Heaven and not towards fellow creatures, even from a lenient to a stringent [prohibition]; and one who is suspected of one matter that is bad towards Heaven and bad towards fellow creatures is suspected of the entire Torah, even [in matters that are] bad towards Heaven and bad towards fellow creatures.

Tosafot on Eruvin 69a:1:1.hebrew: והא תנן מי שנתן רשות כו' - הא דפריך אברייתא טפי מאמתני', משום דבברייתא מסיים בה: "דברי ר"מ":
Tosafot on Eruvin 69a:1:1.english: "But didn’t we learn: One who gave [away] his rights..." etc. - The fact that [the Gemara] raises an objection against the baraita rather than against the mishna is because in the baraita it concludes: "The statement of Rabbi Meir."

Tosafot on Eruvin 69a:3:1.hebrew: הוציא בין בשוגג בין במזיד יכול לבטל - פירש בקונט': אע"ג דמומר הוא לחלל שבת, יכול לבטל. "ר' יהודה אומר: במזיד אינו יכול לבטל" — קסבר: מומר לחלל שבת אינו יכול לבטל בלא שכירות. ומדתולה טעם בקונטרס משום מומר, צריך לומר דבפרהסיא קאמר, כדמסיק: דדוקא בפרהסיא לר' יהודה אינו יכול לבטל רשות, ואפ"ה לר"מ מבטל רשות. ובסמוך נמי, דקאמר: "מומר בגילוי פנים אינו מבטל רשות, כמאן? כר' יהודה" — פירש בקונט': דלר"מ, במומר לחלל שבת בפרהסיא מבטל. ותימה, דבמתני' קתני: "צדוקי הרי הוא כנכרי", כדמסיק לעיל; ומשמע בריש פירקין דרישא דמתני' ר"מ! וי"ל: דודאי כולה מתניתא עד ר' יהודה, ר"מ קתני לה, כדמסיים בה בברייתא "דברי ר"מ" — דר"מ שונה דברי רבותיו: דברי חכמים ודברי ר"ג; ואפשר דסבר כר"ג, דאמר: "צדוקי אינו כנכרי". ועוד, מדפליגי ר"מ ור' יהודה אליבא דר"ג, משמע נמי דכר"ג סבירא ליה. ומיהו לא משמע כלל לפרש ברייתא זו מטעם מומר: חדא, דלמה ליה למנקט "הוציא"? הוה ליה למימר "שחילל שבת", בכל מלאכה שחילל! ועוד, דמשמע דמשום דהוציא בשבת זו — דקתני: "עד שלא נתן רשותו הוציא"! ועוד, דמשמע סתם "הוציא" בכל ענין, בין בצנעא בין בפרהסיא — כמו "מי שנתן רשותו והוציא" דסיפא. ומפרש ר"י, דהכא לאו מטעם מומר קאמר, דמומר לא שייך אלא באדם הרגיל לחלל שבתות ואינו נזהר כלל; אבל הכא לא ברגיל איירי, אלא שבמקרה בעלמא אירע כך שהוציא, שהיה דחוק לפי שעה. ואם בשבת שעברה עשה כן, אפי' במזיד, לא היה מזיק כלום, אפי' לר' יהודה — דלאו מומר הוא, כדפירשתי — אלא דוקא בשבת זו, דמאחר שהחזיק ברשותו אינו יכול לבטל, כמו החזיק אחר ביטול דאין יכול עוד לבטל. ור"מ סבר דיכול לבטל, משום דלא חשיב מחזיק, כיון שאחר הנתינה לא החזיק:
Tosafot on Eruvin 69a:3:1.english: If he carried, whether unwittingly or intentionally, he can renounce [his rights] - Rashi explained in the kunteres: Even though he is an apostate regarding desecrating Shabbat, he can renounce [his rights]. "Rabbi Yehuda says: [If he carried] intentionally, he cannot renounce [his rights]" — he holds [that] an apostate regarding desecrating Shabbat cannot renounce [his rights] without renting [out his share]. And since in the kunteres he attributes the reason to [him being] an apostate, one must say that it is speaking [of one who carried] in public (befarhesya), as [the Gemara] concludes: that specifically in public, according to Rabbi Yehuda, he cannot renounce [his] rights, and even so, according to Rabbi Meir, he can renounce [his] rights. And similarly nearby [on 69b], where [the Gemara] says: "An apostate with brazenness [i.e., in public] cannot renounce rights — according to whose [view]? According to Rabbi Yehuda" — Rashi explained in the kunteres: according to Rabbi Meir, in [the case of] an apostate regarding desecrating Shabbat in public, he [nevertheless] renounces [his rights]. And this is astonishing, for in the Mishnah [68b] it teaches: "A Sadducee is considered like a gentile," as [the Gemara] concluded above; and it implies at the beginning of our chapter [61b] that the opening clause of the Mishnah is [the view of] Rabbi Meir! And one can say that certainly the entire Mishnah up until Rabbi Yehuda was taught by Rabbi Meir, as it concludes in the baraita, "This is the statement of Rabbi Meir" — for Rabbi Meir would teach the words of his teachers: the words of the Sages and the words of Rabban Gamliel; and it is possible that he held like Rabban Gamliel, who said: "A Sadducee is not like a gentile." And furthermore, from [the fact] that Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda dispute according to [the view of] Rabban Gamliel, it also implies that he holds like Rabban Gamliel. However, it does not seem at all [correct] to explain this baraita on the basis of [being] an apostate: First, why did it need to use [the term] "carried"? It should have said "desecrated Shabbat," through whatever labor he desecrated! And furthermore, it implies that [the law applies specifically] because he carried on this Shabbat — for it teaches: "Before he gave his rights, he carried"! And furthermore, plain "carried" implies in any manner, whether in private or in public — just like "one who gave his rights and carried" in the latter clause. And Ri explains that here it is not speaking on the basis of [being] an apostate, for [the status of] an apostate applies only to a person who is accustomed to desecrating Shabbatot and is not careful at all; but here it is not dealing with one who is accustomed [to doing so], but rather that merely by happenstance it occurred that he carried, because he was pressed for the moment. And if he had done so on the previous Shabbat, even intentionally, it would not have caused any harm, even according to Rabbi Yehuda — for he is not an apostate, as I explained — but rather specifically on this Shabbat, for since he took possession of his domain, he cannot renounce [his rights], just like one who took possession after renunciation can no longer renounce. And Rabbi Meir held that he can renounce, because he is not considered to have taken possession, since after the giving [of rights] he did not take possession.

Tosafot on Eruvin 69a:6:1.hebrew: כאן במומר לחלל שבתות בפרהסיא - לפירוש הקונט' שהוציא במזיד דלעיל חשיב מומר, אפי' במילי דרבנן. וכן משמע, מדלא משני: הא והא בפרהסיא, הא בדאורייתא הא בדרבנן. ותימה, דהא סתם צדוקי אינו נזהר כלל במילי דרבנן, אפי' בפרהסיא! וכותים נמי, שהיו מבטלים ונותנים רשות קודם שגזרו עליהם ר' אמי ור' אסי בפ"ק דחולין (דף ו:) — הא סתם כותים אינם מאמינים בדברי חכמים, ואפי' בפרהסיא, ולא מזדהרי! וי"ל, שרגילים הם ליזהר לפי שיראים מחכמים, כדאשכחן בנדה פרק בנות כותים (נדה דף לג: אע"פ שצדוקים אנו, מתיראין אנו מפני הפרושים):
Tosafot on Eruvin 69a:6:1.english: Here, [it refers] to an apostate who desecrates Shabbat in public - According to the explanation of the Kuntres [Rashi], that one who carried out intentionally [mentioned] above is considered an apostate even for rabbinic matters — and this is also indicated by the fact that [the Gemara] did not resolve [the contradiction by stating]: "Both this and that [refer to desecration] in public; [yet] this [case involves a] Torah [prohibition], while that [case involves a] rabbinic [prohibition]" — yet this is difficult: for an ordinary Sadducee is not careful at all regarding rabbinic matters, even in public! And Samaritans as well, who would renounce and transfer rights before Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi decreed against them in the first chapter of Chullin (6b) — surely ordinary Samaritans do not believe in the words of the Sages, even in public, and are not careful! And one can say that they are accustomed to be careful because they fear the Sages, as we find in Niddah, chapter Benot Kutim (Niddah 33b): "Even though we are Sadducees, we are afraid of the Pharisees."

Tosafot on Eruvin 69a:9:1.hebrew: כיון דחזיה לר' יהודה נשיאה כסייה - וא"ת: והא ר' יהודה נשיאה גופיה נפק בחומרתא דמדושא, כדאמרי' במועד קטן בפרק מי שהפך (מועד קטן דף יב:)? ותירץ ר"ח: דהאי גברא דהכא נפק ברשות הרבים, והתם — בחצר. ותימה! אפי' בחצר משמע התם דאסור, דקאמר על ר' אמי דאיקפד: מאי טעמא איקפד? אי משום חומרתא דמדושא — והא תניא: "השירים והנזמים והטבעות הרי הן ככל הכלים הניטלין בחצר!" ואמר עלה דההיא ברייתא בסוף פרק כירה (שבת דף מו:): אמר עולא, מאי טעמא? הואיל ואיכא תורת כלי עליהן. ומדנקט טעמא דתורת כלי, משמע דאסור להתקשט בהם בחצר דלא חזו בשבת, ואפ"ה שרי לצורך גופו ולצורך מקומו, כמו כל דבר שיש תורת כלי עליו אע"פ שמלאכתו לאיסור; כדאמר בפרק במה אשה (שבת דף סד:): "כל מקום שאסרו חכמים לצאת בו לרה"ר, אסור לצאת בו לחצר, חוץ מכבול ופאה נכרית!" ואור"י: דודאי שירים ונזמים וטבעות אסור להתקשט בהם בחצר שמא יצא בהן לרה"ר, וברשות הרבים אסור דילמא שליף ומחוי, ולא חשיב גזירה לגזירה. אבל חומרתא דמדושא אינו תכשיט כלל, ואפי' הוציאה באצבעו לחצר ליכא איסור משום תכשיט, דלאו תכשיט הוא, אלא איסור טלטול בעלמא הוא דאיכא — כלשון ראשון שפירש בקונט': "טבעת שחותמה ממין אחר", ולא כלשון ב' שפירש: "קשר של בשמים"; וכן במועד קטן (דף יב:), דמדמה להו לשירים ונזמים וטבעות. ור' יהודה נשיאה לצורך גופו ולצורך מקומו אפקינהו, כגון לטייל בהם את התינוק או שאר עניינים. ומשום הכי קאמר: "מ"ט איקפד?" — דאיסור טלטול ליכא, שהרי יש עליה תורת כלי, כדתניא: "השירים והנזמים", שהם כשאר כלים שמלאכתן לאיסור שניטלין לצורך גופן; וכיון דאיסור טלטול ליכא, איסור תכשיט פשיטא דליכא, דאינו עשוי לתכשיט, אלא כמו עץ בעלמא שעשוי לחתום בה חותמות. ור"ת מפרש: דתרוייהו נפקי לרה"ר — ר' יהודה נשיאה באצבעותיו, וההוא גברא בקומצו. ואם היה מותר לטלטל, היה יכול להתקשט בו לרה"ר, שתכשיט הוא, ולא שייך למגזר באיש שליף ומחוי; לכך לא הוצרך להביא ראיה אלא על הטלטול, דלא חשיב כחתיכה של מתכת או של עץ דעלמא. ומיהו קשה לר"י: דזה היה יכול לדקדק מן מתני' דפ' במה אשה יוצאה (שבת דף נז.), דתנן: "בטבעת שאין עליה חותם לא תצא, ואם יצאה אינה חייבת חטאת", ש"מ דחשיב ראויות לתכשיט. ועוד, דלישנא ד"נפק" לא משמע בקומצו:
Tosafot on Eruvin 69a:9:1.english: “When he saw Rabbi Yehuda Nesia, he covered it” - And if you should say: But didn’t Rabbi Yehuda Nesia himself go out with a chummarta demadusha [a seal of madusha wood], as we say in Moed Katan in the chapter [entitled] Mi Shehafakh (12b)? And Rabbeinu Chananel answered that this man here went out into the public domain, whereas there [Rabbi Yehuda Nesia went out] into a courtyard. Yet this is astonishing! For even in a courtyard it implies there that it is forbidden, as [the Gemara] says concerning Rabbi Ami, who was dismayed: “What is the reason he was dismayed? If [it was] because of the chummarta demadusha — but isn’t it taught: ‘Bracelets, nose rings, and finger rings are like all utensils that may be moved in a courtyard’?” And Ulla said regarding that baraita at the end of the chapter [entitled] Kira (Shabbat 46b): “What is the reason? Since they have the status of a utensil.” And since he cited the reason of having the status of a utensil, this implies that it is forbidden to adorn oneself with them in a courtyard because they are not fit [for wearing] on Shabbat, and nevertheless it is permitted [to move them] for the sake of their use or for the sake of their place, like anything that has the status of a utensil even though its work is for a forbidden purpose — as [the Gemara] states in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Ishah (Shabbat 64b): “Any item with which the Sages prohibited going out into the public domain, it is forbidden to go out with it into a courtyard, except for a woolen cap and a wig”! And Ri says: Certainly regarding bracelets, nose rings, and finger rings, it is forbidden to adorn oneself with them in a courtyard lest one go out with them into the public domain; and in the public domain it is forbidden lest [a woman] remove [her jewelry] and show [it], and this is not considered a decree upon a decree. However, a chummarta demadusha is not an ornament at all, and even if one brought it out on his finger into a courtyard, there is no prohibition on account of ornamentation, since it is not an ornament; rather, there is merely an ordinary prohibition of handling [muktzeh] — according to the first formulation that [Rashi] explained in the Commentary: “a ring whose seal is of a different material,” and not according to the second formulation that he explained: “a packet of spices”; and similarly in Moed Katan (12b), where [the Gemara] compares it to bracelets, nose rings, and finger rings. And Rabbi Yehuda Nesia brought it out for the sake of its use or for the sake of its place, such as to amuse a child with it or for other matters. And for this reason [Rav Yosef] said: “What is the reason he was dismayed?” — for there is no prohibition of handling it, since it has the status of a utensil, as it is taught: “Bracelets and nose rings,” which are like other utensils whose work is for a forbidden purpose, which may be moved for the sake of their use; and since there is no prohibition of handling it, a prohibition of ornamentation is obvious that there is none, for it is not made for ornamentation, but is merely like ordinary wood that is made for stamping seals with it. And Rabbeinu Tam explains that both of them went out into the public domain: Rabbi Yehuda Nesia [wearing it] on his fingers, and that man [carrying it] in his fist. And if it were permitted to be handled, one would be able to adorn oneself with it into the public domain, as it is an ornament, and it is not applicable to decree in the case of a man [lest he] remove it and show it; therefore, [Rav Yosef] did not need to bring proof except regarding handling it, that it is not considered like a mere piece of metal or ordinary wood. However, it is difficult according to Ri: For this could have been inferred from the Mishnah in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Ishah Yotzeah (Shabbat 57a), as we learned: “With a ring that does not have a seal upon it, [a woman] may not go out, and if she went out, she is not liable to bring a sin-offering,” which proves from it that they are considered fit as an ornament. And furthermore, the expression “went out” does not imply [carrying it] in his fist.
